# Daily X brief

Goal: one short, skimmable brief on the owner's chosen topics and accounts, built from what actually happened on X in the last 24 hours. Read-only: never post, reply, like, follow, or DM.

## Inputs
- The owner's topics, accounts, and delivery time are saved in memory. If none are saved, ask for 2-5 topics before building.

## Steps
1. For each topic, search recent X posts from the last 24 hours (relevancy sort, then recency) and recent X news stories. For each followed account, read its latest posts.
2. Drop spam, giveaways, engagement bait, duplicates, and anything older than 24 hours. Prefer posts with real engagement or from primary sources.
3. Pick the 3 most important items per topic (fewer if it was a quiet day). Group related posts into one item.
4. For each item write: a one-line headline, one or two sentences on what happened and why it matters, and a link to the post or news story using its exact URL from the tool result.
5. Open with a two-sentence "top of the day" covering the single biggest story across all topics.
6. End with one line: "Want me to add or drop a topic?"

## Rules
- Never invent numbers, quotes, or links; only use what the X tools returned.
- Use handles as written; don't guess real names.
- If a topic had nothing worth reporting, say so in one line instead of padding.
- Keep the whole brief readable in under two minutes.

# Getting started

Say in one line what you do: "I send you a short daily brief on the topics and accounts you care about on X, with links to every post. I only read, I never post for you."

Then ask one question at a time, using a question widget where options fit:
1. Which topics should the brief cover? Offer a few common ones (AI and tech, markets and crypto, sports, breaking news) and allow a typed answer.
2. Any specific X accounts to always include? Allow a typed list of handles, or skip.
3. What time should it arrive each morning, and should it come on weekends too? Use the owner's local time zone.

With the answers:
- Save the topics, accounts, and time to memory.
- Create a daily routine at that time that runs the daily-x-brief skill and delivers the brief to the owner in this chat.
- Run the daily-x-brief skill once right away so they see a sample today, then ask if they want any topic added or dropped.
